title: H1 injectivity makes the Picard triviality locus open
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $f_i:X_i\to S$ ($1\le i\le n$) be flat, proper morphisms of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $u_i:X_i\to X$ be morphisms over $S$. Assume that for every morphism $T\to S$, the canonical maps $\mathcal O_T\to (f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ and $\mathcal O_T\to ((f_i)_T)_*\mathcal O_{(X_i)_T}$ are isomorphisms [def-pc-base-change, lem-sc-picard-diagonal-locally-closed]. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible module on $X$ [def-sc-invertible-module], let $\mathcal L_i=u_i^*\mathcal L$ be its pullback to $X_i$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and let $Z$ and $Z_i$ be the locally closed subschemes of $S$ representing the loci where $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal L_i$ are pulled back from the base. Assume $Z$ is contained in the scheme-theoretic intersection of the $Z_i$. If $s\in Z$ and the map $H^1(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})\to\bigoplus_i H^1((X_i)_s,\mathcal O_{(X_i)_s})$ induced by the morphisms $u_i$ is injective, then there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $s$ in $S$ such that $Z\cap U$ equals $(\bigcap_i Z_i)\cap U$ scheme-theoretically.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma lemma-H1-O-multiple-picard-flat-proper, Tag 0BF2 (the proof immediately preceding Lemma pic-of-product, Tag 0BF3)

proof.text: Replace the base by the scheme-theoretic intersection of the $Z_i$, and then by an affine neighbourhood of $s$ on which every $\mathcal L_i$ is trivial. The inclusion $Z\subseteq\bigcap_i Z_i$ and the universal Picard-locus construction [lem-sc-picard-diagonal-locally-closed] justify this replacement; the desired equality is now the assertion that $\mathcal L$ becomes pulled back from the base.

source.place: Lemma lemma-H1-O-multiple-picard-flat-proper, Tag 0BF2, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Put $E=Rf_*\mathcal L$ and $E_i=Rf_{i,*}\mathcal O_{X_i}$. The proper flat finite-presentation hypotheses and the universal pushforward assumptions give perfect complexes and arbitrary base-change isomorphisms; in particular the fibre of $E$ at $s$ is $R\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal L_s)=R\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ because $s\in Z$.

source.place: Lemma lemma-H1-O-multiple-picard-flat-proper, Tag 0BF2, definition of E and E_i

proof.text: After shrinking the affine base, apply the finite-free residue model [lem-sc-perfect-finite-free-residue-model] to $E$ and each $E_i$; by step 2 the ranks are $h_j=\dim_{\kappa(s)}H^j(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ and $h_{i,j}=\dim_{\kappa(s)}H^j(X_{i,s},\mathcal O_{X_{i,s}})$, which vanish for $j<0$, and $h_0=h_{i,0}=1$ by the pushforward hypothesis for $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. Since the model of $E$ is a bounded complex of finite free modules on an affine scheme and the model of $E_i$ is a bounded complex of quasi-coherent modules, the map $E\to E_i$ in the derived category (functoriality of $Rf_*$ along $u_i$, compatible with base change) is represented by a chain map $(a_i,b_i,c_i,\ldots)$ between these two fixed models (higher cohomology of quasi-coherent modules on an affine vanishes, so derived-category maps out of a bounded finite free complex are chain maps up to homotopy). The degree-zero residue maps $a_i\otimes\kappa(s)$ are isomorphisms because the chosen fibre trivializing section pulls back to the chosen trivializing section on every $X_{i,s}$.

source.place: Lemma lemma-H1-O-multiple-picard-flat-proper, Tag 0BF2, finite-free complexes and chain-map diagram

proof.text: The injectivity hypothesis on $H^1$ says that the direct-sum degree-one residue map $(b_1,\ldots,b_n):\kappa(s)^{h_1}\to\bigoplus_i\kappa(s)^{h_{i,1}}$ has rank $h_1$. A nonzero $h_1\times h_1$ minor therefore remains invertible after shrinking, so the direct-sum map of free modules is injective (for $h_1=0$ this is vacuous). Since each pulled-back line bundle is trivial, the degree-zero differentials $d_i$ vanish, and the degree-zero maps $a_i$ are isomorphisms after shrinking because their residue maps are. The chain-map identity gives $(\oplus_i b_i)d=(\oplus_i d_i)(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=0$, hence $d=0$ by injectivity.

source.place: Lemma lemma-H1-O-multiple-picard-flat-proper, Tag 0BF2, injective minor and d=0 paragraphs

proof.text: The equality $d=0$ means that the chosen trivializing section of $\mathcal L_s$ lifts to a global section $\sigma$ of $\mathcal L$ on $X$. Its zero locus is closed; by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] its image under the proper morphism $f$ is closed in $S$. Since the zero locus misses the fibre over $s$, an open neighbourhood $U$ of $s$ avoids that image. Thus $\sigma|_{X_U}$ is nowhere vanishing and, by the defining local property of an invertible module, gives a trivialization of $\mathcal L|_{X_U}$. The universal property of $Z$ then identifies $Z$ with the scheme-theoretic intersection of the $Z_i$ on $U.
